chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Muhammad ibn Khalid: that he asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the alms-tax (zakat).

He (the Imam) said, 'Indeed, that will not be accepted from you.' He said, 'I carry that from my wealth.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him, 'Order your collector to not gather from water to water, nor to unite what is scattered, nor to separate what is united. When the wealth enters, let him divide the livestock into two halves and let the owner choose whichever half he wishes; if he chooses, let him give it to him. And if the owner of the livestock desires from the other half a sheep, or two sheep, or three, let him give them to him. Then let him take his alms-tax. When he takes it out, let him appraise it for whomever he wishes. When it stands at a price, if its owner wants it, he is more entitled to it; and if he does not want it, let him sell it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the procedure for dividing and distributing zakat on livestock according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the precise administrative procedure for distributing zakat from livestock, emphasizing the owner's right to select specific animals from the collector's share before the zakat portion is finalized. It highlights the scholarly principle of 'tawqif' (divine specification) in fiqh, where the method of distribution is not merely discretionary but strictly defined by the Imam to ensure fairness and prevent dispute. The process ensures that the zakat is only taken from the remaining balance after the owner's selection, reflecting a nuanced approach to wealth purification in Shia jurisprudence.
